scenario: A translational oncology team studying ipsc derived neurons performs the following experiment: A team builds a cell-state classifier for 50,000 cells from 4 patients (2 responders on Batch A, 2 non-responders on Batch B). They split cells randomly 80/20 (putting cells from the same patient in train and test), select top 1,000 highly variable genes across all 50,000 cells globally, and report 99.8% test accuracy. They collect samples and execute computational modeling.
question: Critique the methodology of this ipsc derived neurons study. Identify any fatal methodological flaws, explain the underlying biological and statistical mechanisms, provide rigorous corrections, and establish whether reported biological claims are warranted.
ground_truth_rationale: Authoritative scientific rationale: Multiple fatal compounding scientific flaws: 1) Patient-level data leakage across train/test splits (pseudoreplication in CV); 2) Complete confounding between batch and clinical response (Batch A=responders, Batch B=non-responders); 3) Global unsupervised feature selection leaking test set variance. The model is classifying patient/batch artifacts, not therapy response. In ipsc_derived_neurons biology, failing to account for this leads to erroneous translational conclusions.
